I've farmed this land for 30 years. I know this soil, I know this weather, and I know what works in Quzhou. My well gives me some control over water, which is good because summers can be dry.

My 10.1 mu splits roughly like this in my head: about 6 mu goes into my wheat-maize rotation — wheat in winter, maize on the same ground in summer. I keep about 4 mu separate for spring potato. That's how I've always done it.

**Wheat:** I'll buy improved certified seed from the county agricultural supply store, same variety I've used the last few years — stable yield, disease tolerant enough. I rotary till after the maize harvest in October to break up the stalks. I apply compound fertilizer as basal before sowing, then topdress urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: once before sowing to get moisture right, once at jointing, once at heading. Two pesticide passes — herbicide in early winter, then aphid and powdery mildew control in April-May.

**Maize:** I always use hybrid seed. 郑单958 or similar. After wheat harvest in June I direct seed into the stubble — no extra tillage, saves time and my back. I push most nitrogen as topdressing at the V6-V8 stage when the plants really need it. Summer rain usually covers part of the irrigation need, so I watch the sky and use the well maybe twice. Two pesticide applications — herbicide early, and I check for corn borer.

**Potato:** This plot gets ploughed deep — potato needs loose soil. Improved variety. Potato eats a lot of potassium so I put more K down here than on my other crops. Four irrigations through the growing cycle. Three pesticide passes to keep late blight under control — one bad blight year I lost half the crop, I don't let that happen again.
